_source: Simplified subset of the US Commerce Control List (CCL), 15 CFR Part 774 Supplement No. 1, organized by its 10 categories (0-9). Curated (~18 representative entries) for a portfolio demonstration — NOT the exhaustive list and NOT legal advice. Each entry maps a plain-English product space to a control classification.

_control_levels.controlled: Fully / tightly controlled — a license is required to nearly all destinations (product-driven).
_control_levels.dual-use: Dual-use — controlled for many destinations; license need depends heavily on destination and end-use.
_control_levels.uncontrolled: Not on the control list (EAR99-style) — generally no license required on product grounds alone.

categories.name: Encryption / information-security software
categories.reason: Information-security items using strong cryptography are controlled for national-security and anti-terrorism reasons and are restricted to most destinations by default (though license exceptions like ENC exist).

categories.name: Cryptographic hardware / secure comms equipment
categories.reason: Cryptographic hardware is controlled for national-security/anti-terrorism reasons across most destinations.

categories.name: Telecommunications interception / monitoring equipment
categories.reason: Interception and surveillance gear is tightly controlled for national-security and human-rights (crime-control) reasons.

categories.name: High-performance computers
examples: high-density compute server exceeding performance thresholds
categories.reason: Computers above certain performance thresholds are dual-use (potential weapons-design / cryptanalysis use); license need is destination-dependent.

categories.name: Advanced computing chips / AI accelerators
categories.reason: Advanced computing ICs and AI accelerators above set thresholds are controlled (advanced-node semiconductor / AI controls), with strict destination-based licensing.

categories.name: Semiconductor manufacturing equipment
examples: advanced etch/deposition tool for chip fabs
categories.reason: Equipment for producing advanced semiconductors is tightly controlled for national-security reasons.

categories.name: Nuclear materials, facilities & equipment
categories.reason: Nuclear-related items are among the most tightly controlled goods (non-proliferation), requiring a license to nearly all destinations.

categories.name: Controlled chemicals / precursors
categories.reason: Chemical/biological precursors and agents are controlled for chemical- and biological-weapons non-proliferation reasons.

categories.name: High-speed / specialized imaging cameras
examples: high-speed instrumentation camera above frame-rate thresholds
categories.reason: Certain high-performance imaging sensors are dual-use; license need depends on destination and specifications.

categories.name: High-power / specialized lasers
examples: high-power industrial fiber laser above control thresholds
categories.reason: Lasers above set power/energy thresholds are dual-use (potential directed-energy / weapons applications).

categories.name: Radar systems
categories.reason: Radar systems are dual-use (surveillance and military targeting applications).

categories.name: Inertial navigation / avionics
categories.reason: Precision navigation equipment is dual-use (missile/UAV guidance applications), controlled by destination and grade.

categories.name: Unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) & systems
categories.reason: UAVs above capability thresholds are dual-use (potential military / delivery-system use); consumer toys are typically not controlled.

categories.name: Aerospace propulsion / gas turbine technology
categories.reason: Propulsion technology is tightly controlled (missile-technology and military-aircraft concerns).

categories.name: Numerically controlled machine tools
examples: 5-axis CNC milling machine above precision thresholds
categories.reason: High-precision multi-axis machine tools are dual-use (can manufacture weapons/aerospace parts).

categories.name: Night-vision / thermal imaging
categories.reason: Night-vision and thermal imaging are dual-use (military targeting/surveillance); controlled to many destinations.

categories.name: Advanced materials (composites, alloys)
categories.reason: High-performance materials are dual-use (aerospace/missile structures); controlled by specification and destination.
